messages:
ela: Heads up 1: new cost dashboard in staging shows some tenants with net_unit_cost < 0 for the last 6h. Not a UI bug, signals look real. Anyone seen this pattern before? https://staging.redwood/costs/newview :eyes:
rachel: Negative unit cost usually means credits applied that aren't scoped properly. Could be prefetch credits duplicated across chain links. Quick question: are we attributing cache credits at invocation or host-level?
devin: We emit cache_credit on cache_hit events (host-level). But the billing join is done on invocation_id which joins to route_id. If prefetch creates a host-level credit and multiple invocations link to that host, credits could be multiplied.
ejess: Oof. That explains the per-model negative lines. UX: the rollout comparison default is sorting by raw net cost which hides unit economics. We should default to per-invocation normalized cost for canary views.
ela: Proposed short fix: in the materialized ingestion job, dedupe cache_credit by prefetch_token_batch_id before joining to invocations. Also add a boolean `credit_deduped` column for traceability.
rachel: Agreed. Also add `credit_scope` tag: values {invocation, route, host, prefetch_batch}. That will let the dashboard filter credits by scope and avoid misleading aggregates.
devin: I'll open a tiny producer change to emit prefetch_batch_id in the cache_credit events and a migration that marks existing batch_ids where possible. Will add `credit_deduped` flag as part of the batch job.
ejess: For the dashboard copy: add a tooltip explaining "negative net indicates credits applied at a different aggregation scope; see 'credit scope' filter." PMs keep panicking when they see negative.
infra-bot: job-run: cost-ingest-dedupe v2 started 2026-03-21T15:40:03Z (run id: 20260321-78)
ela: Nice. Follow-ups: (1) Add a small sparkline for "credit_apportionment_ratio" so we can detect when credits are skewed to small tenant sets. (2) For rollout diff mode, show both per-invocation and aggregated views side-by-side.
rachel: One more edge: quota throttles can drop invocations but not cancel prefetch batches, so small tenants under throttle can appear profitable. Need a throttle-aware normalization: divide credits by successful_invocations+0.0001 to avoid zeros.
devin: I'll prototype the dedupe + scope tags this afternoon and post a link to the PR. If it looks clean we can flip staging and update the help text.
ejess: Thanks! Quick meeting in 20 to align on the copy and the default dashboard landing. :calendar:
ela: Thanks team, appreciate the fast turnaround.
